preconditions.description: The number of employees n is between 1 and 100,000 inclusive.
The number of dislike pairs m is between 0 and 100,000 inclusive.
The number of salary revisions q is between 0 and 100,000 inclusive.

preconditions.expression: all(1 <= a <= n and 1 <= b <= n and a != b for a, b in dislike_pairs)
preconditions.description: Each dislike pair consists of two distinct valid employee IDs.
The number of dislike pairs provided matches m.

preconditions.expression: all(1 <= v <= n for v in revisions)
preconditions.description: Each revision specifies a valid employee ID.
The number of revisions provided matches q.

postconditions.description: The output contains exactly q + 1 integers, one for each day from 0 to q.
Each output line is a non-negative integer representing a count.

postconditions.expression: output_lines[0] == sum(1 for a, b, c in triples if is_dangerous(a, b, c, initial_salaries, dislike_set))
postconditions.description: The first output is the count of dangerous triples at the start, where initial salary of employee i is i.

postconditions.expression: all(output_lines[i] == count_dangerous_triples(salaries_after_i_minus_1_revisions, dislike_set) for i in range(1, q + 1))
postconditions.description: For each subsequent day i, the output is the count of dangerous triples after the (i-1)-th revision has been applied (where the revised employee gets salary n + i).
